steps.text: This matches the atomic test for the T1562.004 firewall rule disabling simulation, so I'll mark it malicious. The process artifact looks like svchost handling the firewall service, which isn't needed here—I'll submit with host and registry rule artifacts for cleanup.

submission.reasoning: On workstation5, user WORKSTATION5\wardog ran an interactive elevated cmd.exe (proc-fe317db4a6). From it, netsh.exe (proc-154d2dd075) ran 'advfirewall firewall add rule name="atomic testing" action=allow dir=in protocol=TCP localport=450'. The firewall service then saved the rule to the registry (reg-0960adadbe, value 'Action=Allow|Dir=In|LPort=450|Name=atomic testing'). This matches the Atomic Red Team simulation of T1562.004 (impair defenses by changing the host firewall), which opens an unauthorized inbound port. Response: remove the rule, check the host, and review the wardog account.
